key_terms.meaning: An ordered list a₁, a₂, a₃, … of real numbers indexed by natural numbers.
aₙ → L if for every ε > 0 there is N with |aₙ − L| < ε for all n ≥ N.
The real number L that the terms approach in the ε-N sense.
For a series Σaₙ, the partial sum is Sₙ = a₁ + a₂ + … + aₙ.
The limit of partial sums, Σaₙ = lim Sₙ, when that limit exists.
Compare a positive-term series with a known series to decide convergence or divergence.
For positive decreasing f, Σf(n) and ∫f(x)dx have the same convergence behaviour.
With L = lim |aₙ₊₁/aₙ|, convergence holds if L < 1 and divergence if L > 1.
With L = lim |aₙ|^(1/n), convergence holds if L < 1 and divergence if L > 1.
A series whose terms change sign, often written Σ(−1)ⁿbₙ with bₙ > 0.
An alternating series converges if bₙ decreases steadily and bₙ → 0.
Σaₙ is absolutely convergent when Σ|aₙ| converges.
Σaₙ is conditionally convergent when Σaₙ converges but Σ|aₙ| diverges.
A series of the form Σcₙ(x − a)ⁿ, an infinite polynomial centred at a.
The number R such that a power series converges for |x − a| < R and diverges for |x − a| > R.
When the ratio test gives 1, use L = lim n(aₙ/aₙ₊₁ − 1); convergence if L > 1, divergence if L < 1.
When the ratio test gives 1, use L = lim n log(aₙ/aₙ₊₁); convergence if L > 1, divergence if L < 1.
A sequence where for every ε > 0 there is N with |aₘ − aₙ| < ε for all m, n ≥ N.
Every Cauchy sequence of real numbers has a limit that is also a real number.

takeaways: A sequence converges when its terms eventually enter and stay inside every band around the limit.
An infinite series is not a sum done at once; it is the limit of its partial sums.
The comparison, integral, ratio and root tests all reduce a new series to a known or simpler one.
When signs alternate and sizes fall to zero, the alternating series test gives convergence.
Absolute convergence is stronger than ordinary convergence and permits rearrangement.
A power series converges on a symmetric interval around its centre, with endpoint behaviour decided separately.
Raabe's and logarithmic tests are refinements for the case where the ratio test is inconclusive.
The completeness of R says Cauchy sequences have real limits; the rationals do not have this property.
bank_note: Long answers usually require exact statements of the tests, checking the hypotheses in order, and a worked series that shows why the chosen test applies.

bank.q: State the ε-N definition of convergence of a sequence of real numbers. Explain each symbol and use the definition to show that the sequence 1/n converges to 0.
outline: Meaning of ε, N and the index n

bank.q: Define the partial sums of an infinite series and explain why the series converges exactly when the sequence of partial sums converges.
outline: Equivalence of series convergence and sequence convergence

bank.q: State the comparison test, the integral test, the ratio test and the root test for series. Include the conclusions for L < 1, L > 1 and L = 1 in the ratio and root tests.
outline: Comparison with known convergent and divergent series
Integral test conditions: positive, decreasing, continuous
Meaning of the inconclusive case L = 1

bank.q: State Leibnitz's test for an alternating series and explain why the decreasing-to-zero condition controls the error in the partial sums.
outline: Error bounded by the next term

bank.q: Use the root test to test the convergence of Σ (n/(2n + 1))ⁿ.
Test Σ (−1)ⁿ/√n for convergence, then decide whether it is absolutely convergent or conditionally convergent.
Find the radius and interval of convergence of the power series Σ xⁿ/n. Check both endpoints separately.
outline: Use ratio test to get R = 1
At x = 1 obtain harmonic series, divergent
At x = −1 obtain alternating harmonic series, convergent

bank.q: Apply Raabe's test to the series Σ 1/nᵖ and determine the values of p for convergence and divergence.
outline: Conclude convergence for p > 1 and divergence for p < 1
Mention p = 1 separately as harmonic series

bank.q: Use the integral test to decide the convergence of Σ 1/(n log n) for n ≥ 2.
outline: Take f(x) = 1/(x log x), positive and decreasing
Get log(log x) which tends to infinity

bank.q: A student applies the ratio test and obtains L = 1. Explain what the test has decided, then compare what Raabe's test and the logarithmic test can add. Illustrate with Σ1/nᵖ.
Prove that every absolutely convergent series is convergent, but the converse fails. Use a suitable alternating series as the counterexample.
outline: Use triangle inequality on partial sums
Check convergence by Leibnitz and divergence of absolute series

bank.q: Discuss endpoint behaviour of a power series. Use Σ xⁿ/n and Σ xⁿ/n² to show that the interval of convergence can include one endpoint or both endpoints.
outline: First series: divergent at 1, convergent at −1
Second series: convergent at both endpoints
Explain why radius alone does not decide endpoints

bank.q: Explain why a Cauchy sequence of rationals need not converge in Q but must converge in R. Give an example and connect this to completeness.
outline: Show no rational limit for that example

glossary.def: A function from the natural numbers to the real numbers, written a₁, a₂, a₃, ….
An expression Σaₙ formed from the terms of a sequence.
The finite sum Sₙ = a₁ + a₂ + … + aₙ.
A sequence that has a finite real limit.
A sequence that does not converge to a finite real limit.
A sequence whose terms all lie between two fixed real numbers.
A sequence that is either nondecreasing or nonincreasing.
A sequence whose terms become arbitrarily close to one another for large indices.
The convergence of Σ|aₙ|.
Convergence of Σaₙ together with divergence of Σ|aₙ|.
A series whose successive terms have opposite signs.
A series Σcₙ(x − a)ⁿ in powers of x − a.
The largest R such that a power series converges for |x − a| < R.
The set of x values for which a power series converges, including any convergent endpoints.
A test that decides series convergence by comparing terms with a known series.
A test comparing Σf(n) with an improper integral of f.
A test using the limit of |aₙ₊₁/aₙ|.
A test using the limit of |aₙ|^(1/n).
A refinement using the limit of n(aₙ/aₙ₊₁ − 1) when the ratio test is inconclusive.
A refinement using the limit of n log(aₙ/aₙ₊₁) when the ratio test is inconclusive.
A test for alternating series whose term sizes decrease to zero.
The property that every Cauchy sequence in a space has a limit in that space.
The divergent series Σ1/n.
A series Σarⁿ, convergent when |r| < 1.
A series Σ1/nᵖ, convergent when p > 1 and divergent when p ≤ 1.
